name: Starter: Estonian
about: Estonian cases and word order in real, everyday sentences.

words.mina: I (ma; mu: my; mul: at me, for having, feeling; mulle: to me; mind: me)
words.olema: to be (on: is, are; ei ole: isn't)
words.sina: you, informal singular (sa; su: your; sul: at you; sulle: to you; sind: you)
words.ei: not (ma ei tea: I don't know)
words.minema: to go (kuidas läheb: how's it going)
words.saama: can, to be able to; to get
words.teadma: to know (teada andma: to let know)
words.meeldima: to please (mulle meeldib: I like it)
words.kodu: home (kodus: at home; koju: home, going home)
words.meie: we (me; meil: at us, for having; meid: us; meiega: with us)
words.tulema: to come (sisse tulema: to come in)
words.sõitma: to go (by car, bus or train), to ride
words.sadama: to fall, of rain or snow (sajab vihma: it's raining)
words.andma: to give (teada andma: to let know)

sooviksin.about: A polite way to order or ask for something: Ma sooviksin kohvi.

kuidas-laheb.about: The everyday how are you; with sul (at you) in it: Kuidas sul läheb?

suua-teha.about: süüa tegema, literally to make something to eat, is to cook; after a verb like meeldib it's süüa teha.

vabandage.about: To get someone's attention or say sorry, politely or to more than one; one friend gets Vabanda.

items.text: Üks tee ja üks vesi, palun.
items.means: A tea and a water, please.
wrong: Üks teed ja üks vesi, palun.
Üks tee ja üks vett, palun.
Jah, ma on aitäh. Head aega!
Ei, ma on aitäh. Head aega!

items.means: I have a brother and a sister.
Excuse me, where is the bathroom?
Excuse me, how much is it?
wrong: Vabandage, kui palju see maksab on?
Vabandage, kui palju see on maksab?

items.means: I live in a small house.
My mother goes to the city.
Tomorrow I go to the city.

items.text: Mul on üks õde ja kaks venda.
items.means: I have one sister and two brothers.
wrong: Mul on üks õde ja kaks vend.
Ma on üks õde ja kaks venda.

items.text: Ma ei tea, kus ta elab.
items.means: I don't know where they live.
wrong: Ma ei tean, kus ta elab.

items.means: My mom works at a hospital.
I live in a small apartment.
There's a book on the table.
There's no milk in the fridge.

items.text: Meil on suur köök ja väike rõdu.
items.means: We have a big kitchen and a small balcony.
wrong: Meil on suurt köök ja väike rõdu.

items.text: Kui ma koju tulen, teen õhtusöögi.
items.means: When I get home, I'll make dinner.
wrong: Kui ma koju tulen, teen õhtusöök.

items.means: I'd like a glass of water.
I want something sweet to eat.
I like cooking with my mom.
I eat eggs in the morning.
I'm going to the store to buy bread.
Tomorrow I'm going to work by bus.
The train was ten minutes late.

items.text: Ma ei ole kunagi Pärnus käinud.
wrong: Ma ei ole kunagi Pärnus käin.

items.means: Grandma's waiting for us at the station.
On Saturday we're going to grandma's.
Are you coming to the movies with us?
We're going to the beach this weekend.

items.text: Ma õpin eesti keelt juba aasta aega.
items.means: I've been learning Estonian for a year now.
wrong: Ma õpin eesti keel juba aasta aega.

items.means: What are you doing this weekend?

items.text: Loodan, et homme on ilus ilm.
items.means: I hope the weather's nice tomorrow.
wrong: Loodan, et homme on ilusat ilm.

concept.line: The verb's ending marks the person, so ma, sa and me are often left out: (ma) elan, (sa) elad, (ta) elab, (me) elame, (te) elate, (nad) elavad; ta is he and she alike, and to be is olen, oled, on, oleme, olete, on.
Estonian has no words for a, an or the; context does their work: Ma olen õpetaja; Laual on raamat.

words.means: olen = am; oled = are; ole = be

concept.line: The genitive means of and comes first (isa auto: Dad's car; mu nimi), goes before words like juurde (vanaema juurde: to grandma's), and often marks a whole, finished object in an affirmative clause (Ma teen õhtusöögi; Kas sa saad akna sulgeda?); an affirmative command normally uses the nominative for a whole noun object instead: Pane uks kinni.
A plain yes/no question usually starts with kas (Kas sa räägid inglise keelt?), and a question word like kus, mis or kuidas comes first; Estonian adds no do.

The partitive (kohvi, vett, keelt) is used with verbs that take a partitive object (Ma joon kohvi; Oota mind), for a negated object (Ma ei joo kohvi), for an indefinite amount or none (klaas vett; Külmkapis ei ole piima), and after a basic-form number other than one (kaks venda).

words.means: maja = house; majas = in a house
väike = small; väikeses = in a small
elan = live; elad = live; elab = lives
lähen = go; lähed = are going; läheb = goes

concept.line: Estonian says having with -l and on: Mul on õde (I have a sister, literally at me is a sister); Meil on suur köök; and how you feel: Mul on külm (I'm cold).

words.means: minema = to go; minna = to go
